title: I Interviewed Haley Stevens at 11 PM on Her Fiancé’s Couch. Here’s Why She Broke with Abdul El-Sayed.

I Interviewed Haley Stevens at 11 PM on Her Fiancé’s Couch. Here’s Why She Broke with Abdul El-Sayed.

Congresswoman Haley Stevens realized she could no longer back Abdul El-Sayed less than 24 hours ago. She tells Olivia Reingold what made her change her mind. (Nic Antaya for The Free Press ) The Michigan congresswoman says she endorsed Republican Mike Rogers because ‘I think he loves the country.’ By Olivia Reingold 11.02.26 — U.S. Politics This article is part of Today in America . Follow to get everything we publish on U.S. politics, policy, and the ideas worth fighting for. FOLLOW BUNDLE --:-- --:-- Upgrade to Listen Produced by ElevenLabs using AI narration 551 327 READ IN APP READ IN APP HUNTINGTON WOODS, Michigan — “I was like, wait a moment, what am I doing?”
 That is how Congresswoman Haley Stevens described her epiphany less than 24 hours earlier, when she realized she could no longer back Abdul El-Sayed—the Democratic darling favored to win Michigan’s open Senate seat.
 It’s Sunday night at 11 p.m., and she’s seated on her fiancé’s couch at his home in the Detroit suburbs, fishing around a popcorn bowl while telling me how her discomfort with El-Sayed had been building ever since he beat her in the August primary by fewer than 14,000 votes . 
 “I wasn’t being honest with myself after a certain point,” she said with a shrug.
